Decline push-ups are another modified version of the traditional push-up that target the upper body muscles in a different way. To perform a decline push-up, elevate your feet on an elevated surface, such as a bench, chair, or step, while placing your hands on the ground in a push-up position. Lower your body towards the ground while maintaining a straight line from your shoulders to your ankles, and then push back up to the starting position.

Unlike the inclined push-up, the decline push-up places more emphasis on the shoulders and triceps, while still engaging the chest muscles to a lesser extent. By elevating your feet, you increase the difficulty of the exercise by placing more weight on your upper body, forcing your shoulders and triceps to work harder to push your body back up. The decline push-up can be a great way to challenge your upper body strength and improve your ability to perform other push-up variations. As with any exercise, be sure to use proper form and start with a height that is appropriate for your strength and fitness level.
Preparation
Stand on weight plate, bumper plate, or shallow elevated platform with loaded bar above feet. Squat down and grasp bar with shoulder width or slightly wider overhand or mixed grip.
Execution

Lift bar by extending hips and knees to full extension. Pull shoulders back at top of lift if rounded. Return weights to floor by bending hips back while allowing knees to bend forward, keeping back straight and knees pointed same direction as feet. Repeat.
Comments

Throughout lift, keep hips low, shoulders high, arms and back straight. Knees should point same direction as feet throughout movement. Keep bar close to body to improve mechanical leverage. Grip strength and strength endurance often limit ability to perform multiple reps at heavy resistances. Gym chalk, wrist straps, grip work, and mixed grip can be used to enhance grip. Mixed grip indicates one hand holding with overhand grip and other hand holding with underhand grip. Lever barbell jack can be used to lift barbell from floor for easier loading and unloading of weight plates.

Wrist circles is warm-up exercise, where you rotate your wrists in a circular motion.
They improve mobility and are recommended before exercises such as pull ups, hand stands and other exercises that put pressure on your wrists.
With your palms facing forward, curl the weights up to your shoulders.
Turn your hands so that that your palms downwards and slowly return the weights back down.
Finally face your palms back forward.
Lie on your side with a small towel between your top elbow and your ribs.
Hold a light dumbbell with the elbow bent to 90°, forearm across your belly.
Keeping the elbow pinned, rotate the forearm up toward the ceiling.
Lower slowly.
Anchor a band at shoulder height. Raise your upper arm out to the side to shoulder height, elbow bent 90°, forearm pointing forward.
Rotate the forearm up until it points at the ceiling, keeping the elbow still.
Return slowly.
Set a cable at chest height. Upper arm out to the side at shoulder height, elbow bent 90°.
Rotate the forearm up and back until vertical.
Lower under control.
Lie face down on an incline bench holding very light dumbbells.
Raise the arms in a Y shape, then a T, then pull into a W, squeezing the shoulder blades each time.
Lower slowly between each.
Stand holding light dumbbells, thumbs up.
Raise the arms at about 30° forward of your sides up to shoulder height.
Lower slowly.
Lean forward with one hand on a table, the other arm hanging loose.
Let the arm swing in small circles and side to side by rocking your body, not by using the shoulder.
Lie on your side with the bottom arm in front at shoulder height, elbow bent 90°.
Use the other hand to gently press the forearm toward the floor until you feel a stretch in the back of the shoulder. Hold.
Bring one arm across your chest.
Pull it gently closer with the other arm and hold.
Stand side-on to a wall with the elbow bent 90° and the back of the hand against the wall.
Press outward into the wall without moving and hold.
Stand in a doorway with the elbow bent 90° and the palm against the frame.
Press inward into the frame without moving and hold.
Hold a kettlebell upside down by the handle at shoulder height, elbow under the wrist.
Squeeze hard to keep it balanced and hold.
Hold a plank on your forearms, elbows under your shoulders, body in a straight line.
Without bending your elbows or moving your hips, push the floor away so your upper back rounds up and your shoulder blades spread apart.
Slowly let your chest sink back down between your shoulder blades. That's one rep.
Keep your abs tight and your neck long throughout.
Start in a high plank with straight arms.
Without bending the elbows, let the chest sink between the shoulder blades.
Push the floor away to spread the shoulder blades as far as possible.
Lie on your back holding a dumbbell straight up over your shoulder.
Keeping the arm straight, punch it toward the ceiling by lifting the shoulder blade off the floor.
Lower the shoulder blade back down.
Stand facing away from a cable set at chest height, handle in one hand.
Punch forward and slightly up, reaching the shoulder blade around your ribs at the end.
Return slowly.
Anchor a band behind you at chest height.
Punch forward and reach the shoulder blade forward at the end.
Return slowly.

n: Serratus Wall Slide with Foam Roller
h: Stand facing a wall with your forearms on a foam roller against it.
Roll the forearms up the wall while pushing into it and reaching forward.
At the top lift the arms slightly off the wall, then slide back down.
Hold the end of a landmine barbell at your shoulder.
Press it up and forward, reaching at the top.
Lower under control.
On hands and feet with knees just off the floor, back flat.
Crawl forward moving the opposite hand and foot together.
Kneel holding an ab wheel under your shoulders.
Roll it forward slowly while keeping your back flat.
Pull it back under you using your abs.
Hands on a bench or wall, body straight.
Do a push-up and at the top push further to spread the shoulder blades.
Hang from a pull-up bar with straight arms, shoulders gently engaged.
Hold as long as you can.
Drape two towels over a pull-up bar and grip one in each hand.
Hang with straight arms as long as you can.
Grip towels draped over a pull-up bar.
Pull your chin up toward the bar and lower slowly.
Put on a weighted vest and stand with the balls of your feet on a step or plate, heels hanging off the edge. Hold a rail or wall lightly for balance.
Keep your knees straight but not locked. Lower your heels slowly until you feel a stretch in your calves.
Push through the balls of your feet and rise as high as you can onto your toes. Squeeze and hold for a second at the top.
Lower slowly back to the stretch and repeat. Log only the vest's weight, not your body weight.
Put on a weighted vest and stand on one foot with the ball of the foot on a step, heel hanging off. Hook the other foot behind your ankle and hold a rail or wall lightly for balance only.
Keep the working knee straight but not locked. Lower the heel slowly until you feel a full stretch in the calf.
Push through the ball of the foot and rise as high as you can. Squeeze and hold for a second at the top.
Lower slowly and repeat, then switch legs. Log only the vest's weight, not your body weight, and the reps for one leg.
Sit with your upper arm at your side and your elbow bent to 90 degrees.
Squeeze the dynamometer as hard as you can for about 3 seconds.
Rest, and do 2-3 tries with each hand. Log your best squeeze as the weight (1 rep).
Hold a hand gripper and squeeze it fully closed.
Release slowly. Count reps per hand.
Deadlift a barbell to standing (or from a rack).
Hold it with straight arms for time.
Pinch two smooth weight plates together in each hand.
Walk for time without dropping them.
Put thick grips on dumbbells (or use thick-handled ones).
Hold them at your sides for time.
Push your hands into a bucket of rice.
Open, close, twist and dig the fingers for time.
Put a rubber band around your fingers and thumb.
Spread the fingers open against the band, then relax.
Pick up a heavy kettlebell in each hand.
Walk tall for time or distance.
Hold one heavy dumbbell at your side.
Walk without leaning toward the weight, then switch hands.
Sit at a lat pulldown machine with a straight bar on the top pulley and tuck your thighs under the pads.
Grip the bar palms forward, hands a little wider than your shoulders (forearms about vertical at the bottom).
Lean back slightly, chest up. Pull the bar down to your upper chest by driving your elbows down and back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the bottom, then let the bar rise slowly until your arms are straight.
Attach a neutral-grip (parallel handle) bar with handles about shoulder-width apart to the top pulley; sit with thighs under the pads.
Hold the handles palms facing each other.
Lean back slightly, chest up. Pull the handles down to your upper chest, elbows driving down and slightly in front of you.
Pause, then let the handles rise slowly until your arms are straight.
Lie on your side with hips and knees bent, feet together.
Keeping the feet together, lift the top knee without rolling the hips back.
Lower slowly. Add a band above the knees to make it harder.
Lie on your side with the bottom knee bent and the top leg straight.
Lift the top leg up and slightly back, toes forward.
Lower slowly.
Put a band above your knees or around your ankles and bend slightly at hips and knees.
Step sideways keeping tension on the band. Count steps each way.
On hands and knees.
Lift one bent knee out to the side without shifting your weight.
Lower slowly.
On hands and knees with a flat back.
Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back until level with your body.
Pause, return, and switch sides.
Lie on your back with one knee bent and the other leg straight.
Tighten the thigh of the straight leg and lift it to the height of the other knee.
Lower slowly.
Sit or lie with your leg straight and a small towel under the knee.
Tighten the thigh to press the knee down into the towel and hold.
Lie on your back with legs straight.
Slide one heel toward your buttock, bending the knee as far as comfortable.
Slide it back out.
Loop a band behind your knee, anchored in front of you.
Start with the knee slightly bent, then straighten it fully against the band.
Return slowly.
Lie on your back with a rolled towel under the knee.
Straighten the knee by lifting the heel, keeping the back of the knee on the towel.
Lower slowly.
Sit near the front of a chair, feet flat.
Lean forward slightly and stand up without using your hands.
Sit back down slowly.
Stand holding a support if needed.
Bend the knees slightly (a quarter squat) keeping them over your toes.
Stand back up.
Lean your back against a wall and slide down until your knees are bent (up to 90°).
Hold.
Stand on one leg with a slight bend in the knee.
Hold your balance; close your eyes to make it harder.
Stand holding a support.
Rise up onto your toes, then lower slowly.
Stand with your back against a wall, heels a little in front of you.
Lift your toes and the front of your feet off the floor, then lower.
Sit or lie with your leg straight.
Point your toes away, then pull them back toward you. Repeat.
Sit with your foot off the floor.
Trace the letters of the alphabet in the air with your big toe.
Lie face down.
Squeeze your buttock and lift one straight leg a few inches.
Lower slowly.
Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat.
Squeeze your buttocks and lift your hips until your body is straight from knees to shoulders.
Lower slowly.
Lie on your back with knees bent.
Flatten your lower back into the floor by tightening your stomach and tilting the pelvis.
Relax and repeat.
On hands and knees.
Round your back up toward the ceiling, then let it sag while lifting your head.
Move slowly between the two.
Lie face down with hands under your shoulders.
Push your upper body up, keeping your hips on the floor and your back relaxed.
Lower slowly.
Sit or stand tall.
Glide your chin straight back, making a double chin, without tipping your head.
Hold briefly and relax.
Sit or stand tall with arms at your sides.
Squeeze your shoulder blades back and down together.
Hold briefly and relax.
Stand with your back, elbows and wrists against a wall, arms in a W.
Slide the arms up into a Y keeping contact with the wall.
Slide back down.
Stand arm's length from a wall with hands on it at shoulder height.
Bend your elbows to bring your chest to the wall.
Push back.
Lie on your back holding a stick with both hands.
Raise it overhead as far as comfortable, helping the sore arm with the good one.
Lower slowly.
Place your forearms on either side of a doorway, elbows at shoulder height.
Step through until you feel a stretch across the chest and hold.
Stand on a step on one leg.
Slowly lower the other heel toward the floor by bending the standing knee.
Push back up.
Lie on your back and loop a strap around one foot.
Raise the straight leg until you feel a stretch and hold.
Straighten your arm in front, palm up.
Gently pull the fingers back with the other hand and hold.
Straighten your arm in front, palm down.
Gently bend the wrist down with the other hand and hold.
Lie with a foam roller across your upper back, hands behind your head.
Gently extend backward over the roller, moving it up and down your upper back.
